answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public, time-bound challenge before it may submit work. A rotating beacon publishes an unpredictable signal, and the agent must commit to a response before the challenge closes; later, peers check it against the beacon record. Creating thousands of identities then means locking thousands of tokens and bearing the risk of slashing for invalid responses. A cedar-themed name or fresh key cannot bypass that real, repeated capital cost.
